_meta.margin_definition: R% minus D% (positive = Republican lead). Percentages are of all valid votes for candidates (incl. third-party and write-ins; excl. under/over/blank votes).

counts.counties_with_2024_PRES_note: 3,113 = all county-equivalents except Alaska (state-level only, see notes) and Kalawao County HI (15005, reported with Maui by the source); includes DC (11001) and the 9 CT planning regions.
counts.counties_with_2022_note: Counted in the 2024 key space (3,113 keys). Every county in every state that held a 2022 Senate (34 states, 2,059 counties) or governor (36 states, 2,150 counties) race is covered except Alaska. CT additionally has 8 legacy-county keys (09001-09015) carrying 2022 only; including them the raw key counts are SEN=2067, GOV=2158.

ct_crosswalk.name: Wikipedia, List of municipalities in Connecticut (planning region column), 169 towns

openelections_cross_checks.note: openelections-data-<st> 2022 county files used to cross-validate MEDSL county aggregates (PA, SD, WY agree to within 0.4 pt per county; ND/NM/MI files were incomplete or unlabeled and not used)

sources.official_cross_checks: Statewide D/R vote sums for every 2022 race were compared with certified results (Wikipedia infoboxes / state SOS); all agree to within 0.1 percentage point. See baseline_work/out/validation.txt.

notes: Alaska 2024: source reports 40 State House districts with pseudo-FIPS 02001-02040 (these collide with real borough FIPS such as 02013/02016/02020), so no county-level AK rows are emitted; the state row 02 is the sum of all districts. District rows are preserved under _meta.alaska_2024_house_districts.

Alaska 2022: MEDSL reports by State House district only (no county_fips); state-level only. SEN/GOV figures are first-choice (round-1) tallies of the ranked-choice general; R is the sum of all Republican candidates (Murkowski + Tshibaka + Kelley), D is Chesbro. Final RCV result was Murkowski over Tshibaka.
District of Columbia 2024: source reports 8 wards with pseudo-FIPS 11001-11008; aggregated into the single county-equivalent 11001 and state row 11. Ward rows preserved under _meta.dc_2024_wards.

Connecticut: 2024 (tonmcg) is keyed by the 9 Census planning regions (county-equivalents since 2022, FIPS 09110-09190). 2022 (MEDSL, town-level) is emitted under BOTH keyings: the 8 legacy counties 09001-09015 (as MEDSL reports them) and the 9 planning regions 09110-09190 (towns re-aggregated via the town->council-of-governments crosswalk in _meta.sources.ct_crosswalk). Legacy-county rows carry 2022 only; planning-region rows carry 2024 and 2022. Use whichever matches the TopoJSON vintage (2023+ TIGER = planning regions).
Michigan, New York, Indiana, Arkansas, Idaho (Senate) and California (Senate) 2022 use supplemental county tables instead of MEDSL (see _meta.sources.2022_supplemental for why).

South Carolina: MEDSL lists county-level FAILSAFE/PROVISIONAL pseudo-precinct rows twice; exact duplicates were dropped (after which statewide totals match the certified results, e.g. GOV 988,501 R / 692,691 D).
Idaho: MEDSL 'COUNTY TOTAL' pseudo-precinct rows (which double every county) were dropped.
South Dakota: MEDSL uses the retired FIPS 46113 (Shannon) for Oglala Lakota County; remapped to 46102.
Wyoming: MEDSL labels the Democratic nominee Theresa Livingston as Libertarian; corrected to D (cross-checked against the OpenElections WY county file).
New York / Connecticut fusion voting: votes on minor-party lines (Working Families, Conservative, etc.) for the Democratic/Republican nominee are folded into D/R.
Minnesota DFL, North Dakota Dem-NPL and Vermont Dem/Prog candidates are counted as D.
Louisiana 2022 Senate was an open ('jungle') primary held on the November date: D = sum of all Democratic candidates, R = sum of all Republican candidates.
Utah 2022 Senate had no Democratic nominee (independent Evan McMullin was the main challenger): D = 0 and margin is R minus 0; treat UT SEN baseline margin with care.
Oklahoma 2022 had two Senate races: regular (Lankford) = SEN, special (Mullin, seat up again in 2026) = SEN-S.
Georgia 2022 Senate: November general only (the December runoff is excluded).

Indiana 2022 Senate: MEDSL has precinct data for only part of the state; remaining counties were filled from a supplemental source if listed in _meta.sources.2022_supplemental, otherwise flagged in gaps.
Nevada 'None of these candidates' and write-ins are counted in total_votes (as in official returns); under/over/blank votes are not.
